comparator.name: Arts, Culture and Media
comparator.route: Film and Music with Analysis and Criticism
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 TER defines a 180-EC bachelor. This pathway takes the compulsory Year-1 foundation, the first-listed faculty-wide choice, Film I and Music I; continues Film and Music in Year 2; selects Analysis and Criticism, the first-listed Year-2 faculty-wide choice, Film III, Narrativity Across Media and From Studio to Exhibition; and completes the 30-EC minor, Arts in Practice, Evaluating the Arts, Advanced Seminar Film and thesis. Film and Music are the first two eligible departmental disciplines; Analysis and Criticism represents the broad academic identity. Choices are independent of UCR fit.

candidates.label: Arts Policy, Cultural Entrepreneurship and Society

routeSelection.route: Film and Music with Analysis and Criticism
routeSelection.basis: The generic programme requires two arts disciplines and one framework. Film and Music are the first two eligible departmental disciplines. Analysis and Criticism is the broad cross-arts framework, while Arts Policy and Cultural Entrepreneurship is more professionally specialised. Faculty-wide choices use official order as a neutral tie-break; no choice was made for UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Three alternatives are defensible and the maximum is reached. The closest match owns broad art-and-society, criticism, ethical, arts-education, cross-art and Analysis and Criticism interests (7666, 7670, 7671, 7673, 7674, 7678). Film/literature/media communication (7662, 7665, 7672, 7675) and arts policy/cultural entrepreneurship (7667-7669, 7679) yield distinct feasible curricula. Music (7663, 7676) and theatre/performance (7664, 7677) remain evidenced candidates but are not attempted after the maximum; UCR also lacks dedicated music and performance sequences. Curricular topics support the mapped core and candidates; illustrative and outcome rows remain search-only.

alternatives.label: Arts, Media and Cultural Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines visual art and heritage, literature, film and media with cultural theory, history, sociology, ethics, criticism, creative communication and research. It does not claim music or theatre sequences that UCR lacks.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines visual art and heritage, literature, film and media with cultural theory, history, sociology, ethics, criticism, creative communication and qualitative, historical and art-historical research.
progression: Introductory art history, literary studies, film and media, history and sociology precede advanced museum studies, media and race, film and text, social theory, cultural communication and independent research. The schedule observes the available semesters and develops foundational interpretive work before advanced research and criticism.

alternatives.label: Literature, Film and Cultural Communication
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is dominated by literature, film/media and communication, supported by art history, philosophy and qualitative research.
alternatives.concept: A text, screen and communication route connecting literary interpretation, film and media analysis, adaptation, documentary, rhetoric and creative communication with art history, philosophy and qualitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: This route shifts five courses from the closest match’s sociology, cultural theory and heritage balance into rhetoric, communication, adaptation and screen-focused study. The programmes differ by five courses (37.5 EC) each way, above the floor.
progression: Introductions to literature, media and rhetoric precede advanced film-and-text, media-and-race, literary-meaning, persuasive-communication and creative-communication work. Historical, archaeological, philosophical and qualitative foundations support comparative interpretation. Every course is offered in its assigned semester; there are no unmet formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Arts, Culture, Economy and Society
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines arts and media study with sociology, economics, entrepreneurship, leadership and communication.
alternatives.concept: A policy and cultural-entrepreneurship route studying how arts and culture are produced, organised, financed, communicated and socially embedded, while retaining art, heritage, literature and media analysis.
progression: Business, economics, sociology and Western art history establish the organisational, economic, social and visual foundations in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes every selected course that formally requires it. Introductory sociology and art history precede modern sociology, advanced social theory and advanced museum and heritage work; Introduction to Film & Media precedes Media & Race. The final year consolidates cultural theory, media history and representation, literature, market research, art-historical writing and public rhetoric. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.
alternatives.distinctness: This route adds business foundations, economics, entrepreneurship, leadership, social institutions and cultural communication. It differs from the closest match by 11 courses and from the literature/film route by 13 courses, well above the floor.

notes.text: Groningen Arts, Culture and Media requires sequential study in Film and Music in this pathway, plus Analysis and Criticism, Arts in Practice and a thesis. UCR offers strong related study in film and media, literature, visual art and heritage, cultural analysis, sociology and communication, but it does not offer comparable music or theatre/performance sequences.
